subject: humanities
passage: Neoclassical sculptors of the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries, hoping to revive the art of ancient Greece, carved gleaming white marble figures and praised the purity of unpainted stone, a quality they believed the ancient Greeks had prized. The ancient statues they studied had, for the most part, lain buried or stood exposed to the weather for many centuries. Using ultraviolet light and chemical analysis, researchers have since detected traces of paint on many such statues, sometimes in arrangements indicating patterned clothing, colored eyes, and tinted skin, and the binders and many of the pigments used in ancient paint are known to break down over long periods underground or outdoors. These findings suggest that the neoclassical sculptors ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: would have painted their own figures if suitable pigments had been available to them.
choices.B: were wrong to admire any feature of ancient Greek sculpture.
choices.C: knew that ancient statues had been painted but chose to leave their own works white.
choices.D: may have taken the effects of centuries of decay for the intentions of ancient artists.

explanation.why: Two pieces of information combine. The statues the sculptors studied had spent centuries buried or outdoors, and ancient paint is known to break down in those conditions. The whiteness the sculptors admired as an ancient ideal may therefore have been the result of paint wearing away.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text never suggests that the sculptors lacked pigments or wanted to paint their figures.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The findings concern only the sculptors' belief about unpainted stone, not every feature they admired.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says the sculptors believed the ancient Greeks prized unpainted stone, so they did not know the statues had been painted.
explanation.D: Correct. The paint on the statues had largely broken down over the centuries, so the white stone the sculptors admired probably reflected decay, not the original artists' choices.
